title: Sell Mineral Rights in West Point, AR
primaryKeyword: sell mineral rights west point ar
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in West Point, AR | White County
metaDescription: West Point, AR sits on the eastern edge of the Fayetteville Shale in White County. We check your title and price your mineral interest off real production.
heroLead: West Point sits toward the eastern edge of the Fayetteville Shale, past the dense core drilling further west but still inside acreage that saw activity during the play's expansion.
intro: White County caught Fayetteville Shale development as operators pushed development out from the core counties of Van Buren, Cleburne, Faulkner, and Conway, and West Point's part of the county saw some of that extension drilling. That means well spacing here is generally lighter than in the core, and it's not unusual for a tract near West Point to have never been drilled at all, even if a neighboring section has an active well.

sections.heading: What Drilling Actually Looks Like Near West Point
paragraphs: Because this part of White County was flank rather than core acreage, we check every tract individually against Arkansas Oil and Gas Commission well records rather than assuming production the way we might in Van Buren or Cleburne County. Some West Point-area sections have a well and a real production history; others don't, and that changes how the interest gets priced.

sections.heading: Old Family Land and Fractional Ownership
paragraphs: Most of the mineral ownership we see around West Point traces back to farmland that's been in a family for generations, often split among multiple heirs by the time anyone thinks about selling. We pull the deed and probate history at the White County Circuit Clerk's office in Searcy to confirm exactly what percentage you hold before we make an offer.

faqs.question: There's no well on our land near West Point. Is our mineral interest worth anything?
faqs.answer: Possibly, though it's priced more speculatively than a producing tract. We look at nearby well activity and formation depth to judge realistic drilling potential.

faqs.question: How do I find out if my West Point tract is actually producing?
faqs.answer: We check Arkansas Oil and Gas Commission records and White County deed history to confirm whether your specific tract is pooled into a producing unit.

faqs.question: Several family members inherited shares of the same land. Can you buy just mine?
faqs.answer: Yes, we routinely buy one heir's fractional share without requiring the whole family to sell, provided your percentage is documented.

faqs.question: How quickly can a West Point sale close?
faqs.answer: A clean, single-owner tract can close in a few weeks. Estates or unresolved heirship take a bit longer, but we handle that research rather than passing it back to you.
